Internet Gateway

The topic is now confirmed by the project owner, so the technical article is populated. The canonical ledger status is not promoted until the original published artifact is recovered.

An Internet Gateway gives a VPC a route target for direct internet connectivity, but instances still need the right addressing, routes and security policy.

Architecture / mental model

internet ↔ Internet Gateway attached to VPC ↔ public subnet route table ↔ public-addressed workload

How it works

An Internet Gateway attaches to a VPC and can serve as the target for internet-bound routes. A typical public IPv4 subnet route table includes `0.0.0.0/0 → igw-...`.

That route alone is not enough. An IPv4 instance also needs a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP for direct internet communication, and Security Groups/NACLs plus the guest application/firewall must allow the flow.

This is why 'public subnet' and 'public instance' are related but separate ideas: the subnet may have an internet route while a particular instance has no public address.

Hands-on reference

aws ec2 describe-internet-gateways
aws ec2 describe-route-tables

Verification

Trace a public instance from public IP to subnet route table to attached Internet Gateway, then confirm inbound and outbound security rules and the actual application listener.

Field note / gotcha

Attaching an Internet Gateway does not make every VPC resource public. Reachability still depends on subnet routes, addressing and policy.

Security considerations

Expose only the tier and ports that genuinely require direct internet access. Keep databases and internal services off direct public routes unless the architecture has a defensible reason.

What I learned

Internet access is a chain of explicit decisions, not one checkbox labeled public.
